cluster_summary: Shell command injection vulnerabilities caused by inadequate handling of shell metacharacters in either command construction or input validation. One sub-pattern involves insufficient escaping when building shell arguments, allowing metacharacters to break quoting. Another covers allowlist-based validators that miss certain shell constructs, enabling bypass. A third includes missing or easily bypassed input validation.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Use literal command execution with an arguments array (avoid shell wrapping) or fully escape all shell metacharacters including square brackets, using single quotes where appropriate..

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Use literal command execution with an arguments array (avoid shell wrapping) or fully escape all shell metacharacters including square brackets, using single quotes where appropriate.
sub_patterns.name: Insufficient escaping of shell metacharacters in command arguments
sub_patterns.root_cause: Escaping logic omits certain shell metacharacters (e.g., double quotes inside double-quoted strings, square brackets for globbing) leading to injection when the string is interpreted by a shell.
